entries.why_wrong: A missing `default` case isn't the issue here — `size` is always one of the three recognized strings in this scenario, so there's no unrecognized-value path to worry about. The actual problem is that `case "small"` has no `break`, so it falls through into `case "medium"` and overwrites `price` to 10.

Removing `let price = 0` wouldn't fix anything — that initialization is what gives `price` a defined value before the `switch` runs, and it's harmless. The bug is the missing `break` after `price = 5` in `case "small"`, which lets execution fall through and overwrite the value in `case "medium"`.

Moving `break` before the assignment would just exit the switch before `price` ever gets set, which is worse, not better — `break` has to come after the code you want to run for that case. The real fix is adding the missing `break` after `price = 5` in `case "small"`, since its absence lets execution fall through into `case "medium"`.
